editorial:
Imagine meeting a guy who treats life like one big, funny experiment. That is exactly what you get with Chicho. He is not your typical subject; he is a singer, a thinker, and a bit of a rebel who hates following the rules. The vibe is super relaxed, almost like you are just hanging out with him while he explains his views on the world. Instead of a boring lecture, the film uses his music and quirky personality to show you what it means to live an anarchistic life. It feels less like a formal documentary and more like a long, chatty conversation about freedom.

What really works here is how natural everything feels. The pacing is light, and Chicho's energy keeps you interested even when he gets deep into his philosophy. The best part is seeing him perform his songs, which bring his ideas to life in a way that is easy to understand. If you like people who challenge the status quo, you will love this. Since it is an older gem, you should try to find a high-quality restoration. Adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go if you want the best picture, but streaming it in HD on a platform like Prime Video works great too.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing that Chicho's way of thinking is a lifelong journey rather than a destination. In the final scenes, he continues to sing and talk, proving that his spirit cannot be tamed by society. There is no big shock twist because it is a documentary, but the conclusion leaves you feeling inspired. It ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that anyone can find their own freedom if they just dare to think for themselves.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves eccentric personalities and music with a message.
